title: 2026 - Context-adjusted Player Evaluation for Twenty20 Cricket - Bandyopadhyay
file_name: 2026 - Context-adjusted Player Evaluation for Twenty20 Cricket - Bandyopadhyay.pdf
universal_lens: The framework unifies batting and bowling via a symmetric martingale residual. By mapping run-scoring and run-prevention to a single currency of runs above expectation, it constructs an isomorphic state-space where dynamic programming yields dismissal costs, ensuring all performance metrics are context-adjusted and mathematically comparable. Context-adjusted player evaluation integrates empirical Bayes shrinkage with opposition and role-specific multipliers to produce residual-based performance metrics.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the contextual scoring expectation using empirical Bayes shrinkage on a conditional Poisson maximum likelihood multiplier. This Bayesian hierarchical inference stabilizes thinly sampled contexts by pooling them toward the population mean, providing robust, reproducible priors for player evaluation under uncertainty. GSI employs conjugate Gamma-Poisson posteriors for Bayesian inference on player expectations, using exposure counts as proxies for empirical Bayes estimation.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the Bellman expectation recursion to solve the batting side value function, modeling situational reasoning as a Markov decision process. The engine calculates real-time state transitions, pricing each delivery's outcome against the optimal expected yield given the current wicket and over constraints. GSE models dynamic state transitions in cricket innings using Bellman recursions to compute wicket costs and dismissal-adjusted runs across evolving game states.

primitives.name: Runs Above Expected (RAE)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first, Runs Above Expected (RAE), is the residual between the runs scored on a delivery and a contextual expectation of what an average performer would produce in the same situation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: RAE: dimensionless runs; r_t: runs scored on delivery t (runs); E[r_t|C_t]: expected runs given context C_t (runs).
primitives.assumptions: Contextual expectations are stationary within defined state bins; cohort scoring rates follow a multiplicative log-linear structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when contextual features (e.g., pitch conditions) shift drastically outside the training distribution, causing the expectation model to severely miscalibrate.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to baseball's Weighted On-Base Average (wOBA) residuals or Expected Goals (xG) in football, mapping discrete event outcomes to continuous probabilistic expectations.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute deviation of RAE across high-sample contexts should approach zero.

primitives.name: Conditional Poisson Maximum Likelihood Multiplier
primitives.verbatim_quote: That expectation is a multiplicative log-linear model of the cohort scoring rate, whose per-cell estimator is shown to be a conditional Poisson maximum likelihood multiplier.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \lambda_{c}: expected scoring rate for context c (runs/ball); \hat{\theta}_{c}: multiplicative scaling factor (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Run scoring events within a fixed context can be approximated by a Poisson process; independence of deliveries conditional on the state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs in sparse data regimes (empty cells) where the maximum likelihood estimator becomes undefined without regularization.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSI's generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) for event rate prediction, serving as the foundational kernel for context adjustment.
layer2.telemetry: Deviance reduction compared to a baseline intercept-only Poisson model.

primitives.name: Dismissal Adjusted Runs (DAR)
primitives.verbatim_quote: The second primitive, Dismissal Adjusted Runs (DAR), prices a dismissal in that currency as the runs it forgoes, read off a batting side value function solved by dynamic programming through a Bellman expectation recursion, under observed play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: DAR: runs forgone due to dismissal (runs); V(s): value function of state s representing expected remaining runs (runs).
primitives.assumptions: Future scoring potential depends only on the current state (overs remaining, wickets in hand); optimal play is assumed for the baseline value function.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the underlying transition probabilities (e.g., hazard rates) are non-stationary or heavily influenced by unmodeled external factors like sudden weather changes.

layer2.mapping: Directly isomorphic to win probability added (WPA) calculations in American football, translating a binary terminal event into a continuous loss of future state value.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between DAR and actual innings closure speed.

primitives.name: Martingale Dismissal Residual
primitives.verbatim_quote: The centered quantity is a run-weighted mean zero martingale residual of the dismissal process, so a player is charged only for departing from average behaviour.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: realDAR: realized dismissal cost (runs); xDAR: expected dismissal cost under league hazard (runs); Residual: realDAR - xDAR (runs).
primitives.assumptions: The dismissal hazard rate is accurately estimated at the league level; the sequence of dismissal costs forms a martingale difference sequence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated if players systematically alter their risk profile in a way that decouples the league-wide hazard rate from individual survival probabilities.

layer2.mapping: Functions as a GSE anomaly detection kernel, isolating skill-based deviations from stochastic noise in the dismissal timeline.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of the residual across large cohorts should match theoretical martingale variance bounds.

reasoning_traces.think: The derivation begins by recognizing the fundamental heterogeneity of T20 cricket: a boundary in the powerplay carries vastly different strategic weight than one in the death overs. To isolate true player skill, we must strip away this contextual variance. We define the state space $S$ comprising overs remaining, wickets lost, and current score. For any delivery $t$, let $r_t$ be the runs scored. The core innovation is defining Runs Above Expected (RAE) as $r_t - E[r_t | C_t]$, where $C_t$ encapsulates the micro-context. Estimating $E[r_t | C_t]$ requires navigating sparse data; we employ a multiplicative log-linear model, proving its per-cell estimator aligns with a conditional Poisson maximum likelihood multiplier. To prevent overfitting in rare states (e.g., 19th over, 9 wickets down), we apply empirical Bayes shrinkage, pulling extreme cell estimates toward the global mean. Simultaneously, we must account for the catastrophic cost of a dismissal. Using dynamic programming, we solve the Bellman expectation recursion to derive a value function $V(S)$, representing the expected total runs from state $S$ to the end of the innings. A dismissal transitions the state from $(w, o)$ to $(w+1, o)$, incurring a cost equal to the drop in $V$. This is Dismissal Adjusted Runs (DAR). However, dismissals are stochastic. We center the realized DAR against its expectation (xDAR) derived from a league-wide hazard rate. This centers the metric, creating a mean-zero martingale residual. Finally, summing RAE and the centered DAR yields 'Impact', a unified, symmetric metric placing bat and ball on identical footing.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits deeply from Lindsey's (1963) foundational work on run expectancy in baseball, which first quantified the marginal value of a base hit. It evolves through the modern era of Wins Above Replacement (Baumer et al., 2015), adopting the philosophy of measuring value relative to a replacement-level baseline. In cricket, it responds to the limitations of traditional averages and strike rates, which aggregate over heterogeneous phases. It also parallels expected goals (xG) in football, translating discrete events into continuous probabilistic expectations, but uniquely integrates a dynamic programming component to price terminal events (dismissals) based on future state value rather than just immediate point yield.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The model implicitly constructs a rational agent—the 'average performer'—who maximizes run yield given the constraints of the current state. When evaluating a specific batter, we measure their deviation from this rational baseline. If a batter takes excessive risks in the middle overs, leading to a dismissal with a high DAR, the model penalizes them not just for losing their wicket, but for failing to adhere to the optimal state-transition strategy dictated by the innings phase. Conversely, a bowler who induces dot balls in the powerplay is rewarded for forcing the batter into suboptimal, low-yield state transitions. The framework thus models the game as a continuous博弈 (game) between two agents optimizing conflicting objective functions under shared environmental constraints.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition applies to the collinearity between RAE and DAR. Since aggressive shot selection increases both the probability of high runs (positive RAE) and the probability of dismissal (negative DAR), naive summation could double-count risk-taking behavior. The martingale centering of DAR acts as a partial veto, ensuring that a dismissal consistent with the league hazard for that level of aggression is treated as 'expected' noise. Furthermore, we must veto leakage from pitch conditions; if a sticky wicket inflates dismissal rates globally, the league hazard rate (xDAR) must adapt, otherwise batters are unfairly penalized for surviving conditions that naturally induce high DAR. The empirical Bayes shrinkage serves as a secondary veto against over-interpreting small-sample anomalies in specific contextual bins.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical derivation in pages 25-32 establishes a rigorous foundation for separating signal from noise in T20 batting evaluation. By introducing an era multiplier, the model acknowledges that the underlying state space of cricket evolves temporally; a boundary in 2005 carries different informational weight than one in 2026 due to shifting tactical paradigms and equipment advancements. This necessitates a dynamic normalization layer before any cross-temporal comparison can be valid.

Simultaneously, the application of empirical Bayes shrinkage to assign batters to tiers represents a profound Bayesian integration. It prevents overfitting to small-sample anomalies, pulling extreme observed scoring rates toward the population mean based on a well-defined prior. These tiers then serve as indices for the transition matrices, effectively creating a piecewise-linear approximation of a highly non-linear skill landscape.

The core innovation lies in the explicit modeling of the dismissal hazard. Rather than treating wickets as binary endpoints, the framework treats them as continuous probabilistic drains on the value function, heavily dependent on the match phase. The pooling of these hazards across ten major leagues creates a universal baseline, allowing for the isolation of a batter's true survival skill from the ambient danger of the environment.

Finally, the bifurcation into primary and modified metrics elegantly handles missing data problems. By restricting the geometric refinement (line and length) to a secondary metric, the authors preserve the universality and comparability of the headline statistic while still offering a high-resolution diagnostic tool for environments rich in ball-tracking telemetry.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology inherits deeply from the Moneyball revolution, specifically the transition from counting stats to rate stats, and further to context-adjusted expected values. It parallels the development of WAR in baseball, where park factors and era adjustments were crucial. The use of hierarchical Bayesian models mirrors modern sports analytics' shift away from simple averages toward shrinkage estimators that account for sample size reliability.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the model implicitly reconstructs the decision-making processes of both batters and bowlers. Batters are modeled as agents optimizing run accumulation while minimizing the phase-specific hazard of dismissal. Bowlers, conversely, are agents attempting to maximize that hazard. The tier system captures the strategic alignment between these opposing agents, recognizing that higher-tier batters face correspondingly higher-quality bowling attacks.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises regarding data leakage between the primary and modified metrics. If the geometric refinements in mRAE inadvertently encode information already present in the phase definitions of pRAE, collinearity will artificially inflate the perceived value of the tracking data. Furthermore, applying mRAE to leagues with poor tracking coverage would introduce massive selection bias, violating the assumption of exchangeable observations and corrupting the cross-league comparisons established by the pooled hazard baseline.
